headline_marked: [[Multi-agent systems avoid token bloat]] by sharing memory, not passing context
headline: Multi-agent systems avoid token bloat by sharing memory, not passing context
summary: Traditional multi-agent systems bloat prompts by passing full context. A new memory architecture uses shared memory and 'pass by reference' to cap token budgets, ensuring predictable costs and improved efficiency.
details: Multi-agent systems often face a critical failure mode: token accumulation. Each agent passing its full context to the next rapidly increases prompt size, leading to higher costs, increased latency, and diluted attention for the model.

The core issue is 'passing context by value,' where each agent sends a full copy of everything it knows. The proposed solution is to 'pass by reference,' where agents write output to a shared memory layer and subsequent agents retrieve only the necessary slice, capped by a token budget.

This design makes token reduction a structural property of communication, not an afterthought. It ensures that prompt budgets are bounded regardless of chain length or session accumulation, leading to predictable costs over long deployments. This approach is termed 'TokenOps'.

The shared memory layer is structured into three persistent tiers: episodic (L1), semantic (L2), and procedural (L3). Each tier serves a distinct purpose in managing and storing information for the agents.

The episodic tier (L1) is an append-only log of all session events, serving as the raw source of truth. The semantic tier (L2) holds distilled, cross-session facts, versioned and vector-indexed for retrieval by meaning. The procedural tier (L3) stores reusable, organization-specific skills.

A key rule is that facts flow upward through the tiers, from L1 to L2 to L3, never backward. This architecture ensures that L2 and L3 can always be rebuilt from the raw L1 log, providing robust data integrity and recovery capabilities.

headline_marked: [[Dell 14S launches]] with Intel Wildcat Lake, 23-hour battery, and four colors
headline: Dell 14S launches with Intel Wildcat Lake, 23-hour battery, and four colors
summary: This new 14-inch laptop, announced at IFA 2026, targets students with an aluminum build and starts with 8GB RAM, aiming for an accessible price point below the XPS 13.
details: The Dell 14S, unveiled at IFA 2026, features an aluminum build and Intel Wildcat Lake chips. It promises up to 23 hours of Netflix streaming battery life, targeting students with an affordable option.
This new 14-inch laptop will be available in four distinct colors: linen (beige), dusty rose (pink), washed denim (blue), and velvet green. Configurations can go up to 16GB RAM and a 1TB SSD.

Connectivity includes two USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 ports with DisplayPort and Power Delivery, HDMI 1.4, and a 3.5mm audio jack. Display options range from a 300-nit 1920x1200/60Hz LCD to a sharper 450-nit 2880x1800/120Hz panel.
Student-friendly features include a 1080p webcam with Windows Hello face unlock support. Chip offerings will be the Intel Core 5 320 or Core 7 350, not scaling to Panther Lake like the XPS 13.
While exact pricing is TBD, Dell reps indicated it would be close to the XPS 13’s $700 starting price, yet slightly more accessible. The Dell 14S is expected to release later this fall.
